plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 25% of the book, favoring income and broad index exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
Maintain a significant cash buffer for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a target of ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and concentrating on income and broad index holdings. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 1%, MUU to 3%, and METU to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce broad index concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Buy GEV at 4% of the book, adding a top-scoring scanner setup for growth.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small allocation to leverage.
Keep a cash buffer of approximately 10%.
balanced.read: The balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a high-quality new setup. This approach aims for steady growth with controlled drawdowns, balancing upside potential with risk management.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name mandate.
Add to SOXL, MUU, METU, and SPAL, increasing their allocations to 7%, 6%, 6%, and 6% respectively, to lean into leveraged exposure.
Buy GEV at 6% of the book, adding a top-scoring scanner setup for aggressive growth.
This plan maximizes growth potential by using leverage and concentrating in high-scoring setups.
Maintain a smaller cash buffer of approximately 5%.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware that this approach carries substantially higher risk, including larger potential drawdowns and the impact of leveraged ETF decay/rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 30% of the book, prioritizing income and low drawdown.
This plan focuses on generating steady monthly distributions.
Keep a cash buffer for stability.
income.read: The income plan targets ~1% per month, aiming to park cash for yield. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by removing leveraged and high-beta holdings, focusing on income-generating ETFs and broad index exposure. While prioritizing reliable distributions, remember that these are variable and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
